⚠️ **Work in Progress**: This library is still under construction and contains **bugs and missing features**. Use in production environments is not recommended.


## Shapes

The following shapes are supported by Pangolin:

##### 0-dimensional shapes:
- [`Point`](#point): A point in the plane.

##### 1-dimensional shapes:
- [`Segment`](#segment): Unoriented straight line segment.
- [`OrientedSegment`](#oriented-segment): Oriented straight line segment.
- [`Line`](#line) Infinite straight line.
- [`OrientedLine`](#oriented-line) Infinite oriented straight line.
- [`Ray`](#ray) Half-line.
- [`Polyline`](#polyline) Open polygonal chain, possibly self-intersecting.
- [`MonotoneChain`](#monotonechain) Weakly x-monotone polygonal chain.

##### 2-dimensional shapes:
- [`Halfplane`](#half-plane) A straight line and all points on one side of it.
- [`Triangle`](#triangle) Unoriented triangle.
- [`Rectangle`](#rectangle) Axis-aligned rectangle.
- [`Disk`](#disk) A circle with its interior.
- [`Polygon`](#polygon) Simple polygon.
- [`Convex`](#convex) Convex polygon.
- [`PolygonWithHoles`](#polygon-with-holes) Simple polygon minus a set of disjoint polygonal holes.
- [`PolygonSet`](#polygon-set) A set of regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.
- [`HalfplaneIntersection`](#halfplane-intersection) Intersection of half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.


There are many [predicates](shape_methods.md#predicates) and [other methods](shape_methods.md) supported by all shapes, such as `intersects`, `contains`, `squaredDistance`, `distanceL1`, translation, and scaling.
Shapes may be degenerate, for example when some of their defining points are equal. Degenerate shapes may safely be constructed, and are often constructed by the default constructor that sets all points to the origin. See [Degeneracies](#degeneracies) for what they then mean.

Every shape can be built straight from coordinates, with no [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload.") per vertex. The fixed-size shapes take them as arguments — `pgl.Segment(1, 2, 3, 4)`, `pgl.Triangle(0, 0, 8, 0, 4, 8)` — and the four variable-size ones ([`Polyline`](#polyline), [`MonotoneChain`](#monotonechain), [`Polygon`](#polygon) and [`Convex`](#convex)) take one flat list, read in `(x, y)` pairs:

```python
pgl.Polygon([0, 0, 8, 0, 8, 8, 4, 4, 0, 8])   # same as the list of five Points
```

A sequence of [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload.") is accepted just as well, which is what a computed vertex list usually is; a coordinate list of odd length raises a `ValueError`. Coordinates are exact everywhere: `int`, `fractions.Fraction`, or `"a/b"` strings, never `float`.

All shapes contain their boundaries (that is, they are closed in the topological sense). The boundary of a shape is the *manifold boundary*, that is:

- A point has no boundary.
- The boundary of a 1-dimensional shape is the set of (at most two) extreme points of the curve. The boundary of a segment are its two vertices. The boundary of a ray is its one vertex. A line has no boundary.
- The boundary of a 2-dimensional shape is defined in the usual way. The boundary of a triangle is its perimeter, the boundary of a halfplane is the line that defines it.


### Degeneracies

There are two kinds of degenerate shape, and it matters which one you have.

Some are **well defined**: a triangle with three collinear vertices really is a
segment, a disk of radius 0 really is a point, and every operation on them
answers the limit case. Others are **undefined**: a line through two equal points
has no direction, and a disk through three distinct collinear points could be
either of two half-planes. On an undefined shape every geometric operation is
undefined behavior — any value may come back, though never a crash or a hang.

`isUndefined()` tells the two apart, and every shape has it. The well-defined
collapses are named by:

- `s.isPoint()` / `s.getIfPoint()`: whether the shape covers exactly one point,
  and that point (or `None`).
- `s.isSegment()` / `s.getIfSegment()`: whether it covers exactly one segment of
  positive length, and that segment (or `None`).

Not every shape can collapse in every way, so not every shape has all four.
[`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line."), [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label."), [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label.") and [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line.") have nothing to collapse *to* — a
degenerate one is undefined outright — so they carry only `isUndefined()`. A
[`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label."), [`OrientedSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html "Directed segment preserving source-to-target order plus optional segment label.") or [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label.") can only ever become a point, so they have
no `isSegment`. [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") has `isPoint`/`isSegment` but no `getIf` pair.

A shape that has dropped **below its natural dimension** is entirely boundary
with empty interior. So on it `boundaryContains` coincides with `contains`, while
`interiorContains` and `interiorsIntersect` are always `False`.

```python
t = pgl.Triangle(pgl.Point(0,0), pgl.Point(2,2), pgl.Point(4,4))
t.isSegment()                      # True
t.getIfSegment()                   # (0,0)--(4,4)
t.interiorContains(pgl.Point(2,2)) # False: no interior left
```

A [`MonotoneChain`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html "Weakly x-monotone polyline stored by lexicographically sorted vertices.") or [`Polyline`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html "Open polygonal chain stored in traversal order; may self-intersect.") is the exception worth knowing: a straight one
*is* a segment, so `isSegment()` holds, but a chain is one-dimensional to begin
with and has dropped nothing. It keeps its own boundary (its two extreme
vertices) and its relative interior, and `isDegenerate()` is `False`.

### Point

The [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload.") class template defines a point with x and y coordinates. A point has no boundary and has the point itself as the interior.

```python
p = pgl.Point(7,9)
```

You can read the coordinates of a point `p` as `p[0]` and `p[1]` or [`p.x()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html#ad4a835037f85566d87811a0c23716ce1 "Returns the x coordinate.") and [`p.y()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html#adddf838c3aab69fee39bf5ffb847f72d "Returns the y coordinate."). You can also iterate through the coordinates.

```python
for coord in p:
    print(coord, end = ' ')
print(p)
# Output: 7 9 (7,9)
```

A point has methods:
- [`p.swapped()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html#a313ef4ae28a7d9f0405b6dd455775120 "Returns the point with x and y swapped."): Returns the point with x and y coordinates swapped.
- [`p.dual()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html#a6eff780dd37bb234d722052fa0453f5d "Returns the dual Line."): Returns the dual line $y = ax - b$ for a point $(a,b)$.
- [`p.polar()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html#adfb9d9182a567e05d249f6ce4a124f7d "Returns the polar Line."): Returns the polar line $ax + by = 1$ for a point $(a,b)$. Throws an exception for the origin.

### Segment

The [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label.") class template defines an unoriented straight line segment. The segment always stores the endpoints in increasing order.

```python
s = pgl.Segment(1,2,3,4)
t = pgl.Segment(3,4,1,2)
if s == t:
    print(s, "==", t)
# Output: (1,2)--(3,4) == (1,2)--(3,4)
```

You can read the two endpoints of a segment `s` as `s[0]` and `s[1]` or [`s.min()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#a8ca634e3fec2026ef7a18c4a2652667d "Returns the smallest stored endpoint.") and [`s.max()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#a7ed2bf58648e2eb9b29c349b4762aaca "Returns the largest stored endpoint."). You can also iterate through the endpoints.

```python
s = pgl.Segment(3,4,1,2)
for i in (0,1):
    print(s[i], end = ' ')
for p in s:
    print(p, end = ' ')
# Output: (1,2) (3,4) (1,2) (3,4)
```

The interior of a segment is all the segment except the two endpoints.
```python
s = pgl.Segment(1,0,5,0)
t = pgl.Segment(2,0,2,3)
if s.intersects(t):
    print("Intersect!")
if not s.interiorsIntersect(t):
    print("Interiors do not intersect!")
# Output: Intersect! Interiors do not intersect!
```

A segment `s` has methods such as:

- [`s.midpoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#a6ba4f70a48483f85bb36651d9fa16275 "Returns the midpoint of the segment."): Returns the midpoint.
- [`s.length()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#a8c2640b1515b891d3458b89e2bf852ac "Returns the Euclidean length."): Returns `s[0].distance(s[1])` as `float`.
- [`s.squaredLength()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#ae7e06f6bf41a97e0b9a2e2af80eb442d "Returns the squared Euclidean length."): Returns `s[0].squaredDistance(s[1])`.
- [`s.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#a2d653f0f6dfd0664e8afe91816e262c1 "Returns whether both endpoints coincide."): Returns `s.length() == 0`.
- [`s.isVertical()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#ad93d1387983c7189e9e201382111c87c "Returns whether the segment is vertical."): Returns `s[0].x() == s[1].x()`.
- [`s.isHorizontal()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#a6903b76ac4686b9335f6f116c53f322d "Returns whether the segment is horizontal."): Returns `s[0].y() == s[1].y()`.
- [`s.containsEndpoint(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#a90315b916a47d2356ff1793db49f9d63 "Returns whether the given point is one endpoint."): Returns `s[0] == p or s[1] == p`.
- [`s.collinear(t)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#a98ea3f482d52dec230b1a6ff2832af79 "Returns whether the given point lies on the supporting line."): Returns whether `s` and `t` are on the same line.
- [`s.slope()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#a6104dac8ebf1ae689aad41031b1c853e "Returns the slope of the segment."): Returns `(s[1].y()-s[0].y()) / (s[1].x()-s[0].x())`.
- [`s.parallel(t)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#af8c2ca1c497f63c2d7fdd9c984201ed2 "Returns whether another segment is parallel to this one."): Returns whether `s` and `t` have the same slope value.
- [`s.yAtX(x)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#af4487113eb0a0b25129415b203d39b27 "Returns the value of the y coordinate for a given x, if it exists."): Returns the value of the segment y coordinate at the given coordinate `x` or `None`.
- [`s.xAtY(y)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#afc0fd6524c9dd5b450e9ca6393df79d9 "Returns the value of the x coordinate for a given y, if it exists."): Returns the value of the segment x coordinate at the given coordinate `y` or `None`.
- [`s.asLine()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#a17e749637dd68e87c00a49b75e80f958 "Returns the supporting line."): Returns the line that contains `s`.

- Other methods: [`asHalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#a943b1377c091db0951e8990024ec6677 "Returns the segment as a (degenerate) half-plane intersection."), [`asPolyline`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#aa1cf93051c0a3968e6b42dc9a557fee1 "Returns the segment as a two-vertex polyline."), [`minkowskiErosion`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#a2f6bf7949298620b2a8b766addd2338a "Returns the Minkowski erosion of this shape by another (A ⊖ B)."), [`minkowskiSum`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#a23517d7e093249d57a03b51bc33355f1 "Returns the Minkowski sum of this shape and another (A ⊕ B)."), [`pointInside`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#ac381a6cbc94661fbb3f2e602f3999c78 "Returns a point inside the segment."), [`samePointSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html#abf5d373e3dd6ba95b5ef31209cdfc413 "Tests whether another shape defines exactly the same point set."), ### Oriented Segment

The [`OrientedSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html "Directed segment preserving source-to-target order plus optional segment label.") class template defines an oriented straight line segment. The user chooses the order of the two endpoints, which are named [`source`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a2ed4278927ccabd73b1d99c8f8903f10 "Returns the source endpoint.") and [`target`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a6ed02b384a6f31fd6b4c8671286f7231 "Returns the target endpoint."), respectively.

```python
s = pgl.OrientedSegment(1,2,3,4)
t = pgl.OrientedSegment(3,4,1,2)
if s != t:
    print(s, "!=", t)
# Output: (1,2)->(3,4) != (3,4)->(1,2)
```

You can read the two endpoints of an oriented segment `s` as `s[0]` and `s[1]` or [`s.source()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a2ed4278927ccabd73b1d99c8f8903f10 "Returns the source endpoint.") and [`s.target()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a6ed02b384a6f31fd6b4c8671286f7231 "Returns the target endpoint."). You can also iterate through the endpoints.

```python
s = pgl.OrientedSegment(1,2,3,4)
print(s)
# Output: (1,2)->(3,4)
```

An oriented segment `s` has all methods of the [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label.") class:

- [`s.midpoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a9fcc978c0e1b9d9053f2182da496db20 "Returns the midpoint of the segment."): Returns the midpoint.
- [`s.length()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a003b0ff77fdeaff80dfcd5591f884a8f "Returns the Euclidean length."): Returns `s[0].distance(s[1])` as `float`.
- [`s.squaredLength()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a9314e8f0decc3ea85b2ec04a6bb845d8 "Returns the squared Euclidean length."): Returns `s[0].squaredDistance(s[1])`.
- [`s.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a4dc0c036962ec7a1a9142296de15e64f "Returns whether both endpoints coincide."): Returns `s.length() == 0`.
- [`s.isVertical()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a7193013018c0600c23b9719e9a631247 "Returns whether the segment is vertical."): Returns `s[0].x() == s[1].x()`.
- [`s.isHorizontal()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#ac8af96509cf5232e92b04a02cedcfa46 "Returns whether the segment is horizontal."): Returns `s[0].y() == s[1].y()`.
- [`s.containsEndpoint(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a270cc8f80403c643fd94bc36e9ecff50 "Returns whether the given point is one endpoint."): Returns `s[0] == p or s[1] == p`.
- [`s.collinear(t)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#aeb0cf7ae8f1880e3671599fd760f458b "Returns whether the given point is collinear with the oriented segment."): Returns whether `s` and `t` are on the same line.
- [`s.slope()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a2e104f74709a9c280784291df2e868d0 "Returns the slope of the segment."): Returns `(s[1].y()-s[0].y()) / (s[1].x()-s[0].x())`.
- [`s.parallel(t)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#afba1cca649f1edc93dc94bd69be42ca5 "Returns whether the given segment is parallel to the oriented segment."): Returns whether `s` and `t` have the same slope value.
- [`s.yAtX(x)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a8f66de4ed57d7708e522a0bb1f77b566 "Returns the value of the y coordinate for a given x, if it exists."): Returns the value of the segment y coordinate at the given coordinate `x` or `None`.
- [`s.xAtY(y)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#ae08fd372179c6d2b5d146435c2e3abc8 "Returns the value of the x coordinate for a given y, if it exists."): Returns the value of the segment x coordinate at the given coordinate `y` or `None`.
- [`s.asLine()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#af7700575ec9d0865ab559d3a70b3ab94 "Returns the supporting line without orientation."): Returns the line that contains `s`.


It also has:

- [`s.opposite()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#abd0d595b6568119fd0a07a4ef5f4250b "Returns the opposite orientation of the same geometric segment."): Returns the segment with source and target interchanged.
- [`s.orientation(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a531355c630b3b171d3e7ab41f6842149 "Returns the orientation sign of a point with respect to the segment."): Given a point `p`, returns the orientation sign of `s[0],s[1],p` as an `int`: `0` when they are collinear, `-1` when `s` sees `p` to its right, and `+1` when `s` sees `p` to its left.
- [`s.rightHalfplane()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a16de5b4095b9e58bbd2caa405fe44a7c "Returns the half-plane on the right of the segment direction."): Returns the half-plane defined by all points `p` such that `s.orientation(p) <= 0`.
- [`s.leftHalfplane()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a848ba0978471a2ad0df5e246ecd2d077 "Returns the half-plane on the left of the segment direction."): Returns the half-plane defined by all points `p` such that `s.orientation(p) >= 0`.

It knows how to convert itself with an explicit cast to:
- [`s.asOrientedLine()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a32abd5495bfe740ffcfaead86078214b "Returns the oriented supporting line."): Returns the line that contains `s` and has the same orientation.
- [`s.asRay()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#ab9b6246fac158c6af6fc77f20b713a04 "Returns the ray with the same source and direction."): Returns the half-line that contains `s` and has the same source.

- Other methods: [`asSegment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a839015c7197fe69821533cda01d8136a "Returns the segment without orientation."), [`bbox`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a27d265989a331167765f44b9d859a6c5 "Returns the bounding box of the oriented segment."), [`boundaryContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a31c81c01b377355dbfcd9dd4f02f3fad "Tests whether this shape's boundary contains the other shape (∂A ⊇ B)."), [`contains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#abaafa2a3f5387d07b4797c2933ea4aee "Tests whether this shape contains the other shape (A ⊇ B)."), [`convexHull`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a3cfcda34778527e83cf0d2ebf905c4f9 "Returns the convex hull of the segment's endpoints."), [`crosses`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a20c07ae3def1d7976af11cb18f0e5cbf "Tests whether the two shapes mutually separate each other (each disconnects the other)."), [`distanceL1`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a3b7ea89d712f539e67e785f829d2f6f5 "Returns the Manhattan (L1) distance to the given shape."), [`distanceLInf`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a90dfd6d9b702d80a2757598fd9f7009f "Returns the Chebyshev (LInf) distance to the given shape."), from the end."), [`getIfPoint`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a593348e4db9fdb391d4e1254cb7b030f "Returns the point the segment collapses to, if it does."), [`hausdorffDistanceL1`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#a24eca87c73872ebef717020ba6b87517 "Returns the Manhattan (L1) Hausdorff distance to the given shape."), [`hausdorffDistanceLInf`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedSegment.html#af6d974417644e3bc7cad31abd71ab70f "Returns the Chebyshev (LInf) Hausdorff distance to the given shape."), ### Line

The class template [`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line.") represents an infinite unoriented straight line. A line is stored as any two points it contains, but two lines defined by two distinct collinear points always compare equal. The two points are stored in increasing order.

```python
l1 = pgl.Line(1,2,3,4)
l2 = pgl.Line(2,3,1,2)
if l1 == l2:
    print(l1, "==", l2)
# Output: -(1,2)--(3,4)- == -(1,2)--(2,3)-
```

The defining points may be accessed as in a segment. The interior of a line is the whole line, so [`contains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#a0f408aa140c9bd52f34b2b7569e3d32d "Tests whether this shape contains the other shape (A ⊇ B).") and [`interiorContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#ada10a674bd914aa57d211add8a53dfe8 "Tests whether this shape's interior contains the other shape (A∖∂A ⊇ B).") are equivalent.

A line `l` has some additional methods such as:

- [`l.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#aea48143a2889d294c15306a18bbc382f "Returns whether the defining points coincide."): Returns `l[0] == l[1]`.
- [`l.isVertical()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#a4b206c7339d9e8dd2c13c41de28f2d12 "Returns whether the line is vertical."): Returns `l[0].x() == l[1].x()`.
- [`l.isHorizontal()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#a066e7201c620f1ce7311ca130b6bd672 "Returns whether the line is horizontal."): Returns `l[0].y() == l[1].y()`.
- [`l.slope()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#a65b09754cb121f239f3133a082fbdaeb "Returns the slope of the line."): Returns `(l[1].y()-l[0].y()) / (l[1].x()-l[0].x())`.
- [`l.parallel(t)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#a4fba0a6b1449af25c123a338628d8ae5 "Returns whether another line is parallel to this line."): Returns whether `l` and `t` have the same slope value.
- [`l.halfplaneAbove()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#a68570dbd34b227416c066766c61249ef "Returns the half-plane geometrically above this line."): Returns the half-plane defined by all points `p` that are above the line (larger y-coordinate). If the line is vertical, then it returns the half-plane with smaller x-coordinate. In other words, it returns the half-plane defined by all points `p` such that `pgl.OrientedSegment(l[0],l[1]).orientation(p) >= 0`, noticing that `l[0] < l[1]`.
- [`l.halfplaneBelow()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#aecad497c330e3cfdeac70d0b54bebf3a "Returns the half-plane geometrically below this line."): Returns the half-plane containing `l` and not [`halfplaneAbove`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#a68570dbd34b227416c066766c61249ef "Returns the half-plane geometrically above this line.").
- [`l.dual()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#aa72029be2b77416b240bb2511a8e6e57 "Returns the dual point."): Returns the point $(a,b)$ such that `l` is defined by $y = ax - b$. Throws an exception for vertical lines.
- [`l.polar()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#a9a9a9d07c0d3aafcc6b273bc70dfbb0a "Returns the polar point."): Returns the point $(a,b)$ such that `l` is defined by $ax + by = 1$. Throws an exception for lines through the origin.
- [`l.yAtX(x)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#a7788ca87e20897f7a5a4efe74fd7055c "Returns the y-coordinate of the line at a given x-coordinate, if defined."): Returns the value of the line y coordinate at the given coordinate `x`.
- [`l.xAtY(y)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#a70a94d1e1a7c7bd1108ae00c273fde85 "Returns the x-coordinate of the line at a given y-coordinate, if defined."): Returns the value of the line x coordinate at the given coordinate `y`.

- Other methods: [`asHalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#aaa566fe89740c629cfd9752f31be0ac9 "Returns the line as a (degenerate) half-plane intersection."), [`boundaryContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#a36cd0d13335330379612fbd0a72f0284 "Tests whether this shape's boundary contains the other shape (∂A ⊇ B)."), [`collinear`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#a4cfa4e78e3e5b32c03d28c3982d10fad "Returns whether the line interior contains the given point."), [`crosses`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#a76eec7b766eecde475537034df31286c "Tests whether the two shapes mutually separate each other (each disconnects the other)."), [`distanceL1`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#a151fcdf3d89877652115f0aef06ce8d1 "Returns the Manhattan (L1) distance to the given shape."), end."), [`index`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html#acb7f7b3f4940841503855d09b8947c23 "Returns the smallest index i with (*this)[i] == point, or -1 if no defining point equals ### Oriented Line

The class template [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label.") represents an infinite oriented straight line. An oriented line is stored as any two points it contains but the order matters as the line is oriented from the source to the target point. Two lines defined by two distinct collinear points compare equal if the points are in the same lexicographical order.

```python
l1 = pgl.OrientedLine(1,2,3,4)
l2 = pgl.OrientedLine(2,3,1,2)
if l1 != l2:
    print(l1, "!=", l2)
l2 = l2.opposite()
if l1 == l2:
    print(l1, "==", l2)
# Output: -(1,2)--(3,4)-> != -(2,3)--(1,2)->
#         -(1,2)--(3,4)-> == -(1,2)--(2,3)->
```

The defining points may be accessed as in an oriented segment. The interior of an oriented line is the whole oriented line, so [`contains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#a197af38d52a8dec41b6f3d0850e8a7ef "Tests whether this shape contains the other shape (A ⊇ B).") and [`interiorContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#a9b9427e23d27587f59c32a60dfd6e8ba "Tests whether this shape's interior contains the other shape (A∖∂A ⊇ B).") are equivalent.

An oriented line `l` has methods such as:

- [`l.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#ab0a5530262e75a3f25423ea3f5bf14cd "Returns whether the defining points coincide."): Returns `l[0] == l[1]`.
- [`l.isVertical()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#add58c7c5ce15d56d0d142e7bc145d581 "Returns whether the line is vertical."): Returns `l[0].x() == l[1].x()`.
- [`l.isHorizontal()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#aed8a8d6c00d0366a910bc72a1f646040 "Returns whether the line is horizontal."): Returns `l[0].y() == l[1].y()`.
- [`l.opposite()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#a9bf9b108074f26a0943b5d4cc34d8a67 "Returns the opposite orientation of the same geometric line."): Returns the oriented line with source and target interchanged.
- [`l.slope()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#a31868e82121d74b3016766b5482ebff6 "Returns the slope of the line."): Returns `(l[1].y()-l[0].y()) / (l[1].x()-l[0].x())`.
- [`l.parallel(t)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#af3e4eb23abc25f758b37cb1f5d70a286 "Returns whether the given line is parallel to the oriented line."): Returns whether `l` and `t` have the same slope value.
- [`l.halfplaneAbove()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#aeda2dc46e413a0d34b5cb2a127a29ba5 "Returns the half-plane geometrically above the supporting line."): Returns the half-plane defined by all points `p` that are above the line (larger y-coordinate). If the line is vertical, then it returns the half-plane with smaller x-coordinate. In other words, it returns the half-plane defined by all points `p` such that `pgl.OrientedSegment(l[0],l[1]).orientation(p) >= 0`, noticing that `l[0] < l[1]`.
- [`l.halfplaneBelow()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#ad35665c61b605d8b0057ae774367d7d6 "Returns the half-plane geometrically below the supporting line."): Returns the half-plane containing `l` and not [`halfplaneAbove`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#aeda2dc46e413a0d34b5cb2a127a29ba5 "Returns the half-plane geometrically above the supporting line.").
- [`l.orientation(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#aabcb4586ac2a8cc5c655eaa9f2208bca "Returns the orientation sign of a point with respect to the line."): Given a point `p`, returns the orientation sign of `l[0],l[1],p` as an `int`: `0` when they are collinear, `-1` when `l` sees `p` to its right, and `+1` when `l` sees `p` to its left.
- [`l.rightHalfplane()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#a5b450be0b6c1ebcee8d26b805ba000fb "Returns the half-plane on the right of the oriented line."): Returns the half-plane defined by all points `p` such that `l.orientation(p) <= 0`.
- [`l.leftHalfplane()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#a3d80b03525b963c2255216fb6769ddd0 "Returns the half-plane on the left of the oriented line."): Returns the half-plane defined by all points `p` such that `l.orientation(p) >= 0`.
- [`l.yAtX(x)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#ad7299b16efd66c8a5e620684c240a96e "Returns the y-coordinate of the supporting line at a given x-coordinate, if defined."): Returns the value of the line y coordinate at the given coordinate `x`.
- [`l.xAtY(y)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#a9066c3e2a39cb45346775fe4f985ef72 "Returns the x-coordinate of the supporting line at a given y-coordinate, if defined."): Returns the value of the line x coordinate at the given coordinate `y`.

It knows how to convert itself with an explicit cast to:
- [`l.asLine()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#abb932f7bbe6ceb52cc031c12d8c4558b "Returns the line without orientation."): Returns the line without the orientation.

- Other methods: [`boundaryContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#a2e52ea375be1fb13b67e0256f7945ac0 "Tests whether this shape's boundary contains the other shape (∂A ⊇ B)."), [`collinear`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#a65120372dbe5b2486ae04039b984472a "Returns whether the given point is collinear with the oriented line."), [`crosses`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#a0458bbebfaaa1841bf90a90cded19564 "Tests whether the two shapes mutually separate each other (each disconnects the other)."), [`distanceL1`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#acf5ee045bcc3eef55541dcd73577c966 "Returns the Manhattan (L1) distance to the given shape."), [`distanceLInf`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#ac383baef8ff418c69958b32deab46209 "Returns the Chebyshev (LInf) distance to the given shape."), [`get`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html#af8f8a1643b96fa06d90612e56bd73541 "Cyclic access: same as operator[] but index is taken modulo size(); negative indices wrap ### Ray

The class template [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label.") represents a half-line. A ray is stored as its source endpoint and any other point it contains. Two rays `l1`,`l2` are equal if they have the same source and the other defining point of `l1` is contained in `l2`.

```python
l1 = pgl.Ray(1,2,3,4)
l2 = pgl.Ray(2,3,1,2)
if l1 != l2:
    print(l1, "!=", l2)
l2 = l2.opposite()
if l1 == l2:
    print(l1, "==", l2)
# Output: (1,2)--(3,4)-> != (2,3)--(1,2)->
#         (1,2)--(3,4)-> == (1,2)--(2,3)->
```

The defining points may be accessed as in an oriented segment and may be changed directly. The boundary of a ray is its source.

A ray `l` has methods such as:

- [`l.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a68014d94d2e314877bf4a09aaf39ad39 "Returns whether the defining points coincide."): Returns `l[0] == l[1]`.
- [`l.isVertical()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a05e1dd210bf5c5c3ec92adfceb6d5fa5 "Returns whether the ray is vertical."): Returns `l[0].x() == l[1].x()`.
- [`l.isHorizontal()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#aa75a93acd72c880836337a5b2bae3b9f "Returns whether the ray is horizontal."): Returns `l[0].y() == l[1].y()`.
- [`l.opposite()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a749a6d7a25334d7d452c06c939a1ef24 "Returns the ray obtained by swapping the two stored defining points."): Returns the ray with source and target interchanged.
- [`l.slope()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a93ea798d1e9270ced1a7450346fda9b1 "Returns the slope of the supporting line."): Returns `(l[1].y()-l[0].y()) / (l[1].x()-l[0].x())`.
- [`l.parallel(t)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a31d03810caf016b8b5d4dcc8af4ad61d "Returns whether the given line is parallel to the ray."): Returns whether `l` and `t` have the same slope value.
- [`l.halfplaneAbove()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a00aedab9d7a8015114914fd415645177 "Returns the half-plane geometrically above the supporting line."): Returns the half-plane defined by all points `p` that are above the line (larger y-coordinate). If the line is vertical, then it returns the half-plane with smaller x-coordinate. In other words, it returns the half-plane defined by all points `p` such that `pgl.OrientedSegment(l[0],l[1]).orientation(p) >= 0`, noticing that `l[0] < l[1]`.
- [`l.halfplaneBelow()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#aa8ccb101750ad8b384d3637e9ff74a76 "Returns the half-plane geometrically below the supporting line."): Returns the half-plane containing `l` and not [`halfplaneAbove`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a00aedab9d7a8015114914fd415645177 "Returns the half-plane geometrically above the supporting line.").
- [`l.orientation(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a0cb4c142550a83fb2a46205e3c566bd4 "Returns the orientation sign of a point with respect to the ray."): Given a point `p`, returns the orientation sign of `l[0],l[1],p` as an `int`: `0` when they are collinear, `-1` when `l` sees `p` to its right, and `+1` when `l` sees `p` to its left.
- [`l.rightHalfplane()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a0a101de661262dab7e4bc1e48dffd724 "Returns the half-plane on the right of the ray direction."): Returns the half-plane defined by all points `p` such that `l.orientation(p) <= 0`.
- [`l.leftHalfplane()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a01083ffe650f8b9ffaa393f7574f6005 "Returns the half-plane on the left of the ray direction."): Returns the half-plane defined by all points `p` such that `l.orientation(p) >= 0`.
- [`l.yAtX(x)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#aca8c3ed33fcaafeb3a212cc37b1c51b7 "Returns the value of the y coordinate for a given x, if it exists."): Returns the ray's y coordinate at the given coordinate `x`, or `None` if the ray has no point there.
- [`l.xAtY(y)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a1da16a6f7958862040effa675515dc07 "Returns the value of the x coordinate for a given y, if it exists."): Returns the ray's x coordinate at the given coordinate `y`, or `None` if the ray has no point there.

It knows how to convert itself with an explicit cast to:
- [`l.asLine()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#ae47f5294685f87b606737e49cf1982f9 "Returns the supporting line without orientation."): Returns the line containing the ray.
- [`l.asOrientedLine()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a714c4d79f71316abc554f9b5f832b197 "Returns the oriented supporting line."): Returns the oriented line containing the ray and the same orientation.

- Other methods: [`boundaryContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#aa8fb539f32ed24a3b4ab72249754004c "Tests whether this shape's boundary contains the other shape (∂A ⊇ B)."), [`collinear`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a2cd767b07ca2dd0f031dd7679c68d632 "Returns whether the given point is collinear with the ray."), [`contains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#ae0a3ac3654f116edc50c0b26e6838115 "Tests whether this shape contains the other shape (A ⊇ B)."), [`crosses`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a54b58104cdb1a3bef2fd04d3fcbb1876 "Tests whether the two shapes mutually separate each other (each disconnects the other)."), [`distanceL1`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#ae4f6c732976aca9b3a4d263f7f8a5664 "Returns the Manhattan (L1) distance to the given shape."), [`distanceLInf`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#ab9d136bb4dc01963dac4be687e2f477d "Returns the Chebyshev (LInf) distance to the given shape."), [`get`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a22ddc33b71c1a6893470a05d65a87059 "Cyclic access: same as operator[] but index is taken modulo size(); negative indices wrap from the end."), [`index`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html#a3e9100b021385db17bd0f7e3c010830a "Returns the smallest index i with (*this)[i] == point, or -1 if no defining point equals ### Polyline

The class [`Polyline`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html "Open polygonal chain stored in traversal order; may self-intersect.") represents an open polygonal chain: a sequence of vertices joined in traversal order, with $n - 1$ edges for $n$ vertices and no closing edge back to the first vertex. Unlike a [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices."), it may cross itself.

The constructor keeps the vertex order you give it, canonicalizing only the *direction* (the sequence is reversed when the reversal compares lexicographically smaller), so a polyline equals its own reverse but not a different traversal of the same vertices:

```python
p = pgl.Polyline([0, 0, 2, 2, 2, 0])
print(p)
# Output: Polyline[(0,0),(2,2),(2,0)]
print(p == pgl.Polyline([2, 0, 2, 2, 0, 0]))
# Output: True  (the same chain, traversed backwards)
```

Like [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices.") and [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices."), a polyline stores a lazy translation, so translating it is $O(1)$; it is mutable and therefore unhashable.

A polyline `p` has methods such as:

- [`p.isSimple()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a109775a30d3c17acb2b610e5139a17ee "Tests whether the polyline is simple (it does not touch or cross itself)."): Returns true if the chain does not touch or cross itself. A *closed* polyline (last vertex equal to the first) is not simple.
- [`p.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a3c7ecb999d35c0430c7ec57468f9d9d1 "Checks if the polyline is degenerate (all vertices are equal, so it covers at most a single point)."): Returns true if every vertex coincides.
- [`p.length()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a9317b71453005525d3e6d20309478119 "Computes the Euclidean length of the polyline (the sum of its edge lengths)."): Returns the Euclidean length (a `float`: a sum of square roots is irrational in general).
- [`p.lengthL1()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#aa07788cbfbca38496e4920d9a6cbc827 "Computes the Manhattan (L1) length of the polyline.") / [`p.lengthLInf()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a6a8eb393f3ee27522fc9de7d3601475a "Computes the Chebyshev (LInf) length of the polyline."): Return the exact Manhattan / Chebyshev length.
- [`p.pointInside()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#aac18f99afe9c98f8da82d38f804cbe70 "Returns a point inside the polyline."): Returns an exact point in the relative interior (the midpoint of the first edge).

As a 1-dimensional shape, its boundary is its two extreme vertices and its relative interior is everything else — the same convention as [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label."). [`p.intersection(s)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a615fbb18098d3774821bd2b932203c02 "Returns the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B), empty when they are disjoint.") returns a *list* of [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload.") and [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label.") pieces, since a chain can meet even a line in arbitrarily many disjoint places. It is not defined against [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label.") or [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices.").

- Other methods: [`bbox`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a0f6e26a628acedb87aada9fb34159c89 "Computes the bounding box of the polyline."), [`boundaryContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#aa4d5c3d3cf700d00e22da815a4a426de "Tests whether this shape's boundary contains the other shape (∂A ⊇ B)."), [`contains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polyline.html#a8d0533b6ff156b2ee349a702b9d6c403 "Tests whether this shape contains the other shape (A ⊇ B)."), ### MonotoneChain

The class [`MonotoneChain`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html "Weakly x-monotone polyline stored by lexicographically sorted vertices.") represents a weakly x-monotone polygonal chain. Its vertices are stored sorted lexicographically (smaller x first, ties broken by smaller y), which means the constructor treats its input as a **point set**, not as a pre-linked chain: the points are sorted and deduplicated, so any input order yields the same chain, and the chain is automatically simple.

Consecutive vertices may share an x-coordinate, producing a vertical edge — that is what makes it only *weakly* monotone.

```python
c = pgl.MonotoneChain([2, 2, 0, 0, 1, 3])
print(c)
# Output: MonotoneChain[(0,0),(1,3),(2,2)]  # sorted, whatever the input order
print(c.isStrictlyMonotone())
# Output: True  # no two vertices share an x, so the chain is the graph of a function
```

The sorted order buys $O(\log n)$ vertical queries, which no other shape has. Each returns `None` when the query x lies outside the chain's x-extent:

- [`c.indexAtX(x)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a393d5b3cc782e79a7036ee3beb72257f "Locates the vertex or edge of the chain at a given x-coordinate."): The index of the vertex at `x`, or of the vertex starting the edge spanning `x`.
- [`c.yAtX(x)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a9f8a70bee1528bc6809112b9916fae85 "Evaluates the y-coordinate of the chain at a given x-coordinate."): The exact y-coordinate of the chain at `x`.
- [`c.isBelow(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a4bc4bcb2b9210d4d4d320556798ee343 "Tests whether the chain passes weakly below a point.") / [`c.isAbove(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a9eaf22f78515682edac8b3b1590615f1 "Tests whether the chain passes weakly above a point."): Engaged when a ray shot straight down / up from `p` hits the chain. A point *on* the chain satisfies both.
- [`c.isStrictlyBelow(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#ab4111e9c8705101090ac65c78f108feb "Tests whether the whole chain lies strictly below a point at its x.") / [`c.isStrictlyAbove(p)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a1dea6225dd09e3ef817b8d348852b326 "Tests whether the whole chain lies strictly above a point at its x."): The strict variants. A point on the chain satisfies neither.

It is also the only chain that can grow: [`c.insert(point)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a5cd1ec77da22ad3d957149d51e3d8a05 "Extends the chain to contain the given point as a vertex.") or [`c.insert(points)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a5cd1ec77da22ad3d957149d51e3d8a05 "Extends the chain to contain the given point as a vertex.") splices new vertices into the sorted sequence (a duplicate is ignored).

Otherwise it behaves exactly like a [`Polyline`](#polyline): $n - 1$ edges, `Segment`'s boundary convention, a lazy $O(1)$ translation, mutable and therefore unhashable, `length`/`lengthL1`/`lengthLInf`/`pointInside`, and a list-valued `intersection` that is not defined against `Disk` or `Polygon`.

- Other methods: [`asPolyline`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a23a554720f90426584ee46171426d514 "Returns the chain as a polyline traversing its vertices in lexicographic order."), [`bbox`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a8dac08a30c2d04f9fed863e81f8ba4cf "Computes the bounding box of the chain."), [`boundaryContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a5a5cc531b6bc964dbc4ee96e404aae87 "Tests whether this shape's boundary contains the other shape (∂A ⊇ B)."), [`contains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a5ca0039a7ceff302c988f0ee2fca3226 "Tests whether this shape contains the other shape (A ⊇ B)."), [`convexHull`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#aeafc3ad5c15c84621fd03b9665822514 "Returns the convex hull of the chain's vertices."), [`crosses`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#ac70944fe81641ed674b8a30e44f246c1 "Tests whether the two shapes mutually separate each other (each disconnects the other)."), [`diameter`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a216d0b9490b2e2805ff7caa35950a14e "Returns a segment realizing the diameter (the farthest vertex pair)."), [`distanceL1`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a9b90faf34bce85e9bca85890240ba658 "Returns the Manhattan (L1) distance to the given shape."), [`distanceLInf`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a055799497d4803c75814af39f0770a41 "Returns the Chebyshev (LInf) distance to the given shape."), [`edges`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1MonotoneChain.html#a92e90f9bcdbfc6e904af497d5663da47 "Returns the edges of the chain."), ### Half-Plane

The class template [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line.") is stored as an oriented line, but represents a completely different geometric object that contains all points on its left half-plane. The boundary of the half-plane is the line that defines it. Two half-planes are equal if the corresponding oriented lines are equal:

```python
h1 = pgl.Halfplane(1,2,3,4)
h2 = pgl.Halfplane(2,3,1,2)
if h1 != h2:
    print(h1, "!=", h2)
# Output: ^-(1,2)--(3,4)-^ != ^-(2,3)--(1,2)-^

h2 = h2.opposite()
if h1 == h2:
    print(h1, "==", h2)
# Output: ^-(1,2)--(3,4)-^ == ^-(1,2)--(2,3)-^
```

Halfplane does not have an [`intersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#a6ed9f14e8935b883ccf281944f6c9d06 "Returns the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B), empty when they are disjoint.") method. The defining points may be accessed as in an oriented segment and may be changed directly.

A half-plane `h` has methods such as:

- [`h.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#ae962754a791826b988b39273a9e0da7e "Returns whether the defining points coincide."): Returns `h[0] == h[1]`.
- [`h.isVertical()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#a86a553f8847f65c8e89fe1a612ffcfe3 "Returns whether the boundary line is vertical."): Returns `h[0].x() == h[1].x()`.
- [`h.isHorizontal()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#ae4b2bac2a079079c00870916a7c93b0f "Returns whether the boundary line is horizontal."): Returns `h[0].y() == h[1].y()`.
- [`h.opposite()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#a4bcdbe04bd9d5f266d6c1bdf0bc2ad9e "Returns the complementary half-plane with reversed boundary orientation."): Returns the half-plane with source and target interchanged.
- [`h.slope()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#aea8e2495979f8da401683ed157578993 "Returns the slope of the boundary line."): Returns `(h[1].y()-h[0].y()) / (h[1].x()-h[0].x())`, possibly negative.

It knows how to convert itself with an explicit cast to:
- [`l.asLine()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#ade5884b09f45d35c46a09f9cf90c32b6 "Returns the boundary line without orientation."): Returns the line bounding the half-plane.
- [`l.asOrientedLine()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#ade8b1566d820ead8ec0d5865c2d46d3c "Returns the oriented boundary line."): Returns the oriented line bounding the half-plane.

- Other methods: [`asHalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#adbae0b62cd68d80f8654467a0fb9a229 "Returns the half-plane as a half-plane intersection."), [`boundaryContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#abdafb4b982b7a9ae9fdbc587c0bb8503 "Tests whether this shape's boundary contains the other shape (∂A ⊇ B)."), [`contains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#aa856d60bab5d2988ac376a3d15a0453e "Tests whether this shape contains the other shape (A ⊇ B)."), [`crosses`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#ab94d5650f2cc974f8a123ce29bec2bd0 "Tests whether the two shapes mutually separate each other (each disconnects the other)."), [`distanceL1`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#a680fd9297fdcaf1f06c60ec3f37e6a38 "Returns the Manhattan (L1) distance to the given shape."), [`distanceLInf`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#a371048d4b3a901d1e06ff0f3e799a3df "Returns the Chebyshev (LInf) distance to the given shape."), [`get`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#a77cfc9646566571ab9271b538d71132c "Cyclic access: same as operator[] but index is taken modulo size(); negative indices wrap from the end."), [`index`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#a27001adb22631bfa0a96debd380e5ee0 "Returns the smallest index i with (*this)[i] == point, or -1 if no defining point equals point."), [`interiorContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#a295982b670d6e2fed6bea923f846ba2d "Tests whether this shape's interior contains the other shape (A∖∂A [`minkowskiSum`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#a84ca6f0db65730365dc441c97fd88f62 "Returns the Minkowski sum of this shape and another (A ⊕ B)."), [`pointInside`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html#a27a12a9125ffbaa3462d19ae663382c0 "Returns a point inside the halfplane."), ### Triangle

The class template [`Triangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html "Closed triangle stored by three vertices.") is stored as three points, called vertices, which are kept in the following order. The first vertex is the smallest lexicographically and the other two vertices are ordered such that the triangle is oriented counterclockwise (positive orientation test). Two triangles are equal if they have the same vertices.

```python
t = pgl.Triangle(3,3,4,1,1,1)
print(t)
# Output: <(1,1)(4,1)(3,3)>
for i in {0,1,2}:
    print(t[i], end=' ')
# Output: (1,1) (4,1) (3,3)
for p in t:
    print(p, end=' ')
# Output: (1,1) (4,1) (3,3)
for s in t.edges():
    print(s, end=' ')
# Output: (1,1)--(4,1) (3,3)--(4,1) (1,1)--(3,3)
for s in t.orientedEdges():
    print(s, end=' ')
# Output: (1,1)->(4,1) (4,1)->(3,3) (3,3)->(1,1)
```

A triangle `t` has methods such as:

- [`t.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#ab159614e587f6dc4a75789f98fb7a848 "Tests whether the three vertices are collinear."): Returns true if there are equal vertices or all vertices are collinear.
- [`t.centroid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#af601a145a531947ed2b4475ab0102f78 "Returns the arithmetic centroid."): Returns the centroid.
- [`t.circumcircle()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a0b9e50f4c10a634c4706884ff2894fb7 "Returns the circumcircle of the triangle."): Returns the circumcircle.
- [`t.isRectangle()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a4cfb7d8fffa11293343c535bc4825e3f "Tests whether the triangle has a right angle."): Returns whether one angle is 90 degrees.
- [`t.isObtuse()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a7848d637384e479a97395489bf9a61fb "Tests whether the triangle has an obtuse angle."): Returns whether one angle is greater than 90 degrees.
- [`t.isIsosceles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a3cc30d928e1cb21c99eae9765f38e3d4 "Tests whether two sides have the same length."): Returns whether two sides have the same length.

It knows how to convert itself with an explicit cast to:
- `(pgl.Polygon) t` or [`t.asPolygon()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#aaa078dd16798d8d58bb3cb46f64aba3b "Returns the triangle as a simple polygon."): Returns the polygon representation of the triangle.
- `(pgl.Convex) t` or [`t.asConvex()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#ab01b4c98a0859edd28f1961012ff1447 "Returns the triangle as a convex polygon."): Returns the convex polygon representation of the triangle.

- Other methods: [`a`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a49e6b3ba0db01d986087b842b54d9131 "Returns the first vertex."), [`area`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a7d9d7443fe0e474c2a40cc81eeda5aa3 "Returns the non-negative area of the triangle."), [`asHalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a744d2bc25c735a0a4eef875d281706b6 "Returns the triangle as a half-plane intersection."), [`asPolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a01231798c43a25e66d0f7269c94f2020 "Returns the triangle as a one-component set of regions."), [`asPolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#abe42baab6be8b188613e10bda0b5866f "Returns the triangle as a hole-free region."), [`b`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a2940bbceda1e86124340be582ae78283 "Returns the second vertex."), [`boundaryContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a7b7065114ca1f45e385600fb5fcb6530 "Tests whether this shape's boundary contains the other shape (∂A ⊇ B)."), [`c`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#ae3d2e34092959e6f78dbd305910f34ac "Returns the third vertex."), [`contains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a14847b8bcb9746337a5dc06ce8a1209b "Tests whether this shape contains the other shape (A ⊇ B)."), [`convexHull`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#ab01880b8da51364caf3e4863fb53af69 "Returns the convex hull of the triangle's vertices."), [`crosses`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html#a7ff30d2b4490e2f5d8ba3204e71337f6 "Tests whether the two shapes mutually separate each other (each disconnects the other)."), ### Rectangle

The class template [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners.") represents an axis-aligned rectangle. While it is stored internally as only two vertices (minimum and maximum x and y coordinates), it behaves as a polygon with four vertices. It can be constructed from two opposite corners (given as two [`Point`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Point.html "Two-dimensional point with optional label payload.")s or four coordinates), from an iterable of points (it computes their bounding box), or from an iterable of bounded shapes — even of mixed types — in which case it computes the bounding box enclosing them all. Unbounded shapes ([`Line`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Line.html "Unoriented infinite line."), [`OrientedLine`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1OrientedLine.html "Directed infinite line with left/right side semantics plus optional line label."), [`Ray`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Ray.html "Half-infinite line starting from one source point plus optional ray label."), [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line.")) have no bounding box and are rejected.

```python
r = pgl.Rectangle([pgl.Point(1,3),pgl.Point(2,4),pgl.Point(3,1),pgl.Point(5,4),pgl.Point(2,3)])
# Same as pgl.Rectangle(pgl.Point(1,1), pgl.Point(5,4)) or pgl.Rectangle(pgl.Point(1,4), pgl.Point(5,1))
print(r)
# Output: [(1,1),(5,4)]
print(r.min(), r.max())
# Output: (1,1) (5,4)
for i in {0,1,2,3}:
    print(r[i], end=' ')
# Output: (1,1) (5,1) (5,4) (1,4)
for p in r:
    print(p, end=' ')
# Output: (1,1) (5,1) (5,4) (1,4)
for s in r.edges():
    print(s, end=' ')
# Output: (1,1)--(5,1) (5,1)--(5,4) (1,4)--(5,4) (1,1)--(1,4)
for s in r.orientedEdges():
    print(s, end=' ')
# Output: (1,1)->(5,1) (5,1)->(5,4) (5,4)->(1,4) (1,4)->(1,1)
```

A rectangle `r` has methods such as:

- [`r.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a380388f13b2cd9a5ad8f4f806e31be84 "Returns whether the rectangle has empty interior."): Returns true if the rectangle has null area.
- [`r.centroid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a553634d0d486ae85ec22c6a036855f0e "Returns the centroid of the rectangle."): Returns the centroid.
- [`r.circumcircle()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a96f720c89b9116686118e6085374a7ab "Returns the circumcircle of the rectangle."): Returns the circumcircle.

It knows how to convert itself with an explicit cast to:
- [`r.asPolygon()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#af850885808c25c90aaa04506cc1f1537 "Returns the rectangle as a simple polygon."): Returns the polygon representation of the rectangle.
- [`r.asConvex()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a9c20bb08763579e119ea85d68a907ab3 "Returns the rectangle as a convex polygon."): Returns the convex polygon representation of the rectangle.

- Other methods: [`area`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a2edf35e30a352a900730b7531dfc9d22 "Returns the rectangle area."), [`asHalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html#a1a0b079dcd04f043d44ac2c233a08794 "Returns the rectangle as a half-plane intersection."), ### Disk

The class template [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label.") represents a circle with its interior. Disks are stored internally as three boundary points, in the same way as a [`Triangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html "Closed triangle stored by three vertices."). This choice may be surprising, as the standard representation for disks is a center point and a radius. The main motivation is that the circumcircle of a triangle may be represented exactly for integers. Nevertheless, the constructor accepts both forms:

```python
d1 = pgl.Disk(pgl.Point(1,1), pgl.Point(2,5), pgl.Point(4,3))  # Disk from 3 points
d2 = pgl.Disk(pgl.Point(2,3), 4)             # Disk from a point and a radius
print(d2)
# Output: Disk((-2,3)(6,3)(2,7))  # Output always uses 3 points
```

Disk does not have the [`intersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a21e0cb8c11c045cddeccbe886d46ea86 "Returns the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B), re-dispatching through the wrapper's own intersection.") method and cannot be scaled on a single axis. A disk `d` has methods such as:

- [`d.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a19e32c8b7656bfe02982c8a40ea0ff57 "Returns whether the three boundary points are collinear."): Returns true if the points are collinear or equal.
- [`d.radius()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a69765084e501902a81583032fdb7c816 "Returns the center in this disk's exact coordinate type."): Returns the radius length.
- [`d.squaredRadius()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a0027c4ab0d85b7ff3e5b0d5b42b1745f "Returns the squared radius in an explicitly chosen result type."): Returns the squared radius.
- [`d.center()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#a01f21dd5b971164474843df4ad71bfc1 "Returns the center (circumcenter of the three boundary points) in an explicitly chosen coordinate type."): Returns the center point.
- [`d.diameter()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html#ad7c86ba7778cf349bcb6c653e0470ba5 "Returns a segment defining a diameter of the disk."): As always returns a diameter [`Segment`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Segment.html "Unoriented closed segment between two endpoints plus optional segment label."), but for disks the segment is always horizontal.

### Polygon

The class template [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices.") represents a simple polygon. It can be constructed for any number of points in a container that must be given in the order they appear on the polygon. The vertices are accessed in counterclockwise order starting from the minimum vertex (minimum x, breaking ties by minimum y). ~~Internally, the polygon is stored as multiple x-monotone polylines for improved performance.~~

A polygon `P` has methods such as:

- [`P.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#af1d297b10aee661458543c2f5fa00645 "Checks if the polygon is degenerate (has zero area)."): Returns true if the polygon has null area.
- [`P.isSimple()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a5e182cf106f6be5ed3fb49c07daf80c6 "Tests whether the polygon is simple (its boundary does not touch or cross itself)."): Returns true if the edges only intersect at the endpoints of consecutive edges. Takes $O(n \log n)$ time for $n$ edges.
- [`P.isConvex()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a4fd2d656a5e668f8679db56d2d7d5257 "Tests whether the polygon is convex."): Returns true if the polygon is convex, possibly with vertices subdividing convex hull edges. Takes $O(n)$ time.
- [`P.chainCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a298e7f17d9c815d290436c1fea464ea0 "Counts the maximal lexicographically monotone chains the boundary decomposes into, without building any of them."): The number of lexicographically monotone chains the boundary breaks into — 2 for a convex ring, and more the more often the boundary reverses direction in $x$. It is what the containment and intersection tests price themselves on: they run chain against chain when there are few and fall back to a plane sweep when there are many.
- [`P.untangle()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#ab85503d835bc7afa41dedd1140caa1dc "Makes the polygon simple in place by uncrossing its boundary."): Makes the polygon simple in place, returning `None`. Edges that cross are flipped, and when a flip is blocked by collinear vertices the offending vertex is removed instead, so the vertex set may shrink. On return [`P.isSimple()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a5e182cf106f6be5ed3fb49c07daf80c6 "Tests whether the polygon is simple (its boundary does not touch or cross itself).") holds. Worst-case complexity is high.
- [`P.pointInside()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a01d3ae4bdc2b2e560f0c6e4c9e95b78d "Returns a point strictly inside the (simple) polygon."): Returns an exact point strictly inside the polygon, even a non-convex one (the vertex average would not do: it can fall in a notch, outside the polygon).
- [`P.triangulation()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a55c6ba6ed18502faa4cebbe7e15c60ae "Builds the constrained Delaunay triangulation of this polygon.") / [`P.triangulation(segments)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a55c6ba6ed18502faa4cebbe7e15c60ae "Builds the constrained Delaunay triangulation of this polygon."): Returns the constrained Delaunay [`Triangulation`](data_structures.md#triangulation) of the polygon, optionally with extra constrained edges.
- [`P.isStarShaped()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#ae30790ed670ac303737ab4768528d494 "Tests whether the polygon is star-shaped."): Returns true if some point of the polygon sees every other point of it.
- [`P.getStarShapedKernel()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a40f50170a8a36d31d59f66fcd2753f6c "Returns the kernel: the set of points that see the whole polygon."): Returns the *kernel* — every point that sees the whole polygon — as a [`HalfplaneIntersection`](#halfplane-intersection), or `None` when the polygon is not star-shaped. For a convex polygon the kernel is the polygon itself.
- [`P.asPolygonWithHoles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#ae4dbc2d7bc8b01702980d8023abddd76 "Returns the polygon as a hole-free region."): Returns the polygon as a hole-free [`PolygonWithHoles`](#polygon-with-holes) region.

A [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices.") also carries the [boolean operations](shape_methods.md#boolean-operations) [`difference`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a26dfe1b17a6dd113e2e94bd2e66e4297 "Returns the regularized set difference of the two shapes (A ∖ B)."), [`regularizedUnion`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a3066fa00a91b8fa642125c56b8a2d5b7 "Returns the regularized union of the two shapes (A ∪ B).") and [`symmetricDifference`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a8bad6b985b5387cba210ab3ba3ca58a8 "Returns the regularized symmetric difference of the two shapes (A △ B).") — each answering with a [`PolygonSet`](#polygon-set) — and the region-returning [Minkowski sum](shape_methods.md#minkowski-sum). It has `regularizedIntersection` only against a shape that can hold the answer, a `PolygonWithHoles` or a `PolygonSet`.

- [`P.empty()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#af47294488e6bbe647f6e39d0f3f0200c "Returns whether the polygon is the empty set of points."): Returns true if the polygon has no vertex at all, which is the empty set. Distinct from [`isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#af1d297b10aee661458543c2f5fa00645 "Checks if the polygon is degenerate (has zero area)."), which is a polygon with vertices but no area.
- [`P.convexPartition()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#ad5dae65a5c3ecde435146c8e316275f4 "Cuts this polygon into convex pieces with disjoint interiors."): Cuts the polygon into [`Convex`](#convex) pieces with pairwise disjoint interiors whose union is the polygon, using at most four times the fewest pieces possible. Shorthand for `P.triangulation().convexPartition()`.
- [`P.convexCovering()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#af837b0342dd324eaa0163ce47c27436a "Covers this polygon with convex hulls derived from triangle cliques."): Covers the polygon with [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices.") pieces, which may overlap. Irredundant but not necessarily minimum.
- [`P.visibilityGraph()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a2486c5f87a836c247d28fc5260e673be "Returns the visibility graph of the polygon vertices."), [`P.clearVisibilityGraph()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a31ffed2f5e3df9aa9a682e410201b69c "Returns the clear visibility graph of the polygon vertices."), [`P.reducedVisibilityGraph()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#add9e8b8ce20f931b5e84eb54f74e1e34 "Returns the reduced visibility graph of the polygon vertices."), [`P.visibleVertices(q)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#aaf3c63e9821b14fdcdc0584f032d9c43 "The polygon vertices visible from query."), [`P.clearlyVisibleVertices(q)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a3a42aa5a22262e155d7062ae83615ad1 "The polygon vertices clearly visible from query."), [`P.regularizedVisiblePolygon(q)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a9b5a5245f11a6874270912af605f1373 "The part of the polygon visible from query, regularized."): [Visibility](algorithms.md#visibility) inside the polygon.

`P` is not convex in general, so it has neither a Hausdorff distance nor
`verticesContain` (use `P.index(point) is not None` for the latter).

- Other methods: [`area`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#ad4765e3f6390f06a59f25fef4fcb219f "Computes the area of the polygon."), [`asPolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html#a66107f64a7d5194bb7da8d93d809e8a6 "Returns the polygon as a one-component set of regions."), ### Convex

The class template [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices.") represents a convex polygon. It can be constructed for any number of points in a container and will construct the convex hull. The vertices are stored in counterclockwise order starting from the minimum vertex (minimum x, breaking ties by minimum y). If the container already has the vertices in order, a second constructor parameter can be set to true to avoid computing the convex hull.

A convex polygon `c` has methods such as:

- [`c.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a460c2cbe73f75e60d0153be2acb1662d "Checks if the convex polygon is degenerate (has zero area)."): Returns true if the convex polygon has null area.
- [`c.centroid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#ad4000c6649317b13e2695a209d9102e8 "Computes the centroid of the convex polygon."): Returns the centroid.
- [`c.insert(point)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a573355b49f7a15907cd3dec3ac3e8624 "Enlarges the convex polygon so that it contains the given point.") / [`c.insert(points)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a573355b49f7a15907cd3dec3ac3e8624 "Enlarges the convex polygon so that it contains the given point.") / [`c.insert(shape)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a573355b49f7a15907cd3dec3ac3e8624 "Enlarges the convex polygon so that it contains the given point."): Enlarges the hull in place so that it contains the given point, points, or shape. A shape must have vertices to take the hull of, so a [`Disk`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Disk.html "Closed Euclidean disk stored by boundary points plus optional disk label.") and the unbounded shapes raise a `TypeError`. (They are refused explicitly rather than by omission: every shape is iterable over its defining points, so without the guard [`c.insert(disk)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a573355b49f7a15907cd3dec3ac3e8624 "Enlarges the convex polygon so that it contains the given point.") would quietly insert the disk's three *boundary* points, whose hull the disk bulges straight past.)
- [`c.upperHull()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a34084131cdb827a1cf75bdc56e0018de "Returns the upper hull: the boundary chain running from the lexicographically smallest vertex to the lexicographically largest one, clockwise (above the polygon).") / [`c.lowerHull()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a08a0bfcddc1960c1f8ca2f5906730fdf "Returns the lower hull: the boundary chain running from the lexicographically smallest vertex to the lexicographically largest one, counterclockwise (below the polygon)."): Return the upper and lower boundary chains as a [`MonotoneChain`](#monotonechain). Both run between the leftmost and rightmost vertices, and together they cover the boundary.
- [`c.smallestEnclosingDisk()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#ae185416c0a48808775876b8dfdf0fef3 "Returns the smallest closed disk containing the convex polygon.") / [`c.smallestEnclosingRectangle()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#afde56d828ed9a8588eafdce8c1f89213 "Returns the smallest-area rectangle containing the convex polygon."): The smallest enclosing [`Disk`](#disk), and the smallest-**area** enclosing rectangle — which comes back as a [`HalfplaneIntersection`](#halfplane-intersection), since the tightest one is generally tilted and a `Rectangle` is axis-aligned by definition. Both read a convex boundary, which is why they live here; every other shape reaches them through its own `convexHull()`. See [algorithms](algorithms.md#smallest-enclosing-shapes-of-a-convex-hull).

It knows how to convert itself to:
- [`c.asPolygon()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#ab08ccc569a03b8056db708b1f4e26e2f "Returns the convex polygon as a simple polygon."): Returns the polygon representation of the convex polygon.
- [`c.asPolygonWithHoles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a521e736039189d13085ec1e0f846d937 "Returns the convex polygon as a hole-free region."): Returns the hull as a hole-free [`PolygonWithHoles`](#polygon-with-holes) region.
- [`c.asHalfplaneIntersection()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a2c9d6831c71a136d4f2fdba7a74a3eb8 "Returns the convex polygon as a half-plane intersection."): Returns the hull as a [`HalfplaneIntersection`](#halfplane-intersection), one half-plane per edge.

If the convex polygon `c` has $n$ vertices, then:

- [`c.diameter()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#ad44a3c0e434930328c723fcae6c4c7c9 "Returns a segment realizing the diameter (the farthest vertex pair).") takes $O(n)$ time.
- [`c.intersects(s)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a0717c549a9515d6c65cf68e620361239 "Tests whether this shape and the other shape intersect (A ∩ B ≠ ∅).") takes $O(\log n)$ time if `s` is a shape with $O(1)$ vertices (not including Disk).
- [`s.intersects(c)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a0717c549a9515d6c65cf68e620361239 "Tests whether this shape and the other shape intersect (A ∩ B ≠ ∅).") takes $O(\log n)$ time if `s` is a shape with $O(1)$ vertices (not including Disk).
- [`c.intersects(c2)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a0717c549a9515d6c65cf68e620361239 "Tests whether this shape and the other shape intersect (A ∩ B ≠ ∅).") takes $O(\min(n+m) \log(n+m))$ time if `c2` is a convex polygon with $m$ vertices.
- Other predicates take the same time as [`intersects`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a0717c549a9515d6c65cf68e620361239 "Tests whether this shape and the other shape intersect (A ∩ B ≠ ∅).").
- [`c.intersection(c2)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a755f580e0d762c88e0079bce779537ab "Returns the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B), re-dispatching through the wrapper's own intersection.") takes $O((n+m) log (n+m))$ time if `c2` is a convex polygon with $m$ vertices.

- Other methods: [`area`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a75a11db621ea33f8ea69f4946de7034e "Computes the area of the convex polygon."), [`asPolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html#a6ceafa9ef69ed035d3b901438ed7c82f "Returns the convex polygon as a one-component set of regions."),
