### Polygon with Holes

The class [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes.") represents a closed region: a simple outer polygon
minus the **interiors** of a set of polygonal holes. Writing $P$ for the outer
polygon and $H_i^\circ$ for the interior of hole $H_i$,

$$A = P \setminus \bigcup_i H_i^\circ.$$

Every hole must satisfy $H_i \subseteq P$, and distinct holes must have disjoint
interiors — their boundaries may meet. The boundary of $A$ is the boundary of $P$
together with the boundary of every hole. Note that $A$ is connected but its
interior may not be.

This is the shape whose intersections can keep holes, and that is what it exists
for: removing a shape from the middle of another leaves a hole, and no other
shape but a [`PolygonSet`](#polygon-set) — which is made of these — can say so.
Every [boolean operation](shape_methods.md#boolean-operations) answers with a set
of them, and a non-convex [Minkowski sum](shape_methods.md#minkowski-sum) with
one of them or with a set.

```python
outer = pgl.Polygon([0,0, 10,0, 10,10, 0,10])
hole = pgl.Polygon([4,4, 6,4, 6,6, 4,6])
region = pgl.PolygonWithHoles(outer, [hole])
print(region.area(), region.holeCount(), region.vertexCount())
# Output: 96 1 8
```

The outer boundary and every hole are ordinary [`Polygon`](#polygon) values, each
in [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices.")'s own canonical form (counterclockwise, lexicographically smallest
vertex first) — holes are *not* stored reversed. Equality, ordering and hashing do
not depend on the order the holes were given in.

As with [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices."), whose constructor does not check simplicity, structural
validity is a documented precondition rather than an enforced invariant.
[`isValid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#aa97419a7e6b85e7bc47411c68c352131 "Tests the structural contract: every ring simple, every hole inside the outer boundary, hole interiors pairwise disjoint.") checks the whole contract on demand.

A region `A` has methods such as:

- [`A.outer()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a8e97c883e94cc3cfea21a199228b9b19 "Returns the outer boundary."): Returns the outer boundary polygon.
- [`A.holeCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a95fa631cdfb182d4582639f27036ad90 "Returns the number of holes.") / [`A.hasHoles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#af767d2a7dbe8a2b20ce41c5b948a87c2 "Tests whether the region has at least one hole.") / [`A.hole(i)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a2b6447fb67d376262ab25b4dc5a1e8e5 "Accesses a hole by index.") / [`A.holes()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#ae82e3ee3003e31fd957a88a84d3e6ed9 "Returns the holes in canonical order."): The holes, in canonical (sorted) order.
- [`A.addHole(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a765b899d5ff3f411408d7a095df3e0cc "Adds a hole, keeping the canonical order."): Adds a hole in place, keeping the canonical order. A zero-area ring removes nothing and is ignored.
- [`A.eraseHole(i)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a1e2e6aa41d11353728085b52991ccd6f "Erases the hole at the given index.") / [`A.eraseHole(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a1e2e6aa41d11353728085b52991ccd6f "Erases the hole at the given index."): Fills a hole back in, by index or by the polygon itself; the second returns whether it found one.
- [`A.vertexCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#aff0ca302f8ad610564b09c97b15d1ccc "Returns the total number of vertices over all rings."): The total number of vertices over all rings.
- [`A.vertices()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a37281b937de6d6d9317e52d8467b2cba "Returns the vertices of every ring, outer boundary first.") / [`A.edges()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#ae82fd7c3b3450b695607e85c1508976e "Returns the boundary edges of every ring, outer boundary first."): The vertices and boundary edges of every ring, outer boundary first.
- [`A.orientedEdges()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a520a035a55a65cbab4f6fd49fb4a38d9 "Returns the boundary edges directed so the region lies to the left."): The boundary edges directed so the region lies to the left: the outer ring counterclockwise as stored, the hole rings **reversed**.
- [`A.empty()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#ad252b967097b7afea60a29f85d59362b "Tests whether the region has no outer boundary at all."): Returns true if the region has no outer boundary at all, and hence covers no point.
- [`A.isSimple()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#addbf9b8fc422b3358fa22a07f59629a4 "Tests whether every ring is simple."): Returns true if every ring is simple. A per-ring check only: it says nothing about how the rings sit relative to one another.
- [`A.isValid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#aa97419a7e6b85e7bc47411c68c352131 "Tests the structural contract: every ring simple, every hole inside the outer boundary, hole interiors pairwise disjoint."): Tests the whole structural contract above.
- [`A.chainCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#ae174a7bdd8e7f6a81b2b25214d68b9e8 "Total number of maximal lexicographically monotone chains over all rings; see Polygon::chainCount."): The monotone chains of every ring added up, outer boundary and holes together — the same cost measure [`Polygon.chainCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#ae174a7bdd8e7f6a81b2b25214d68b9e8 "Total number of maximal lexicographically monotone chains over all rings; see Polygon::chainCount.") reports.
- [`A.isRegular()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a2e05e6ecb46a97c1fb30a652c59baf23 "Tests whether the region is the closure of its own interior (A = closure(A°))."): Returns true if the region is the closure of its own interior. Since the contract constrains interiors only, a valid region may pinch shut along a whole stretch of edge — a **slit**, region material with no area on either side of it, as when a hole shares an edge with another hole or with the outer boundary. A region with area is regular exactly when it has no slit. Pinching at an isolated *point* is not a slit: the interior still reaches the point from every side.
- [`A.regularized()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a5a58f8d14f3eca262dda7a9cd7b28240 "Returns the region without its slits (closure(A°)), as a set of regions."): Returns $\mathrm{closure}(A^\circ)$ — the region without its slits — as a [`PolygonSet`](#polygon-set), the same regularization every boolean operation applies to its own result. Dropping the slits can disconnect what they were holding together, which is why the result is a set: a region whose slits are its only connective tissue comes back as several components, and one with no area comes back empty.
- [`A.convexPartition()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#ae37b45b249f18d92fbfb5f2fb78bf77c "Cuts this region into convex pieces with disjoint interiors.") / [`A.convexCovering()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#ae4c9367f4e5e4c2df88c48fbe180ce1a "Covers this region with a greedily selected set of convex polygons."): Cut or cover the part of the region that has area with [`Convex`](#convex) pieces. The holes are where there is no piece, and a slit, having no area, appears in none of them.
- [`A.visibilityGraph()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a81b38f56d05ee5980e59b48cf4f175ad "Returns the visibility graph of the region's vertices.") and the rest of the [visibility](algorithms.md#visibility) family: sight is stopped by the outer boundary and by every hole.
- [`A.twiceArea()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a07ab576becc17a6e75abe6aac82c25eb "Computes twice the area of the region.") / [`A.area()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a3ff8504b80feb7b0d457bbf828cc1708 "Computes the area of the region."): Twice the area exactly and without division, and the area itself.
- [`A.centroid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a89865ef96926d3dc0c3099d763b2b694 "Computes the area-weighted centroid of the region."): The area-weighted centroid, the holes entering with negative weight. When the net area is zero the centroid of the vertex set is returned instead.
- [`A.verticesCentroid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a4da4174e8d22a44cd02e9d37490d7321 "Computes the centroid of the vertex set over all rings."): The centroid of the vertex set over all rings.
- [`A.pointInside()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a5aa4c9229ddb2199ba0ea26f025e70cf "Returns a point strictly inside the region."): A point strictly inside the region, so inside the outer boundary and outside every hole. Undefined for a region with no area.
- [`A.triangulation()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#af82e342491cc24b09de583b69c4ef4bf "Builds the constrained Delaunay triangulation of this region.") / [`A.triangulation(segments)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#af82e342491cc24b09de583b69c4ef4bf "Builds the constrained Delaunay triangulation of this region."): The constrained Delaunay [triangulation](data_structures.md#triangulation) of the region. Every ring becomes constrained edges and the hole interiors are left out of the domain, so the in-domain triangles cover exactly the part of the region that has area — a slit, having none, carries no triangle.
- [`A.diameter()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#ab228725f55c314fc60383ffa2b06adfd "Returns a segment realizing the diameter (the farthest vertex pair).") / [`A.bbox()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a030085f5ccf7e57317823cbb2e742be2 "Computes the bounding box of the region."): The holes lie inside the outer boundary and cannot contribute, so both are the outer polygon's.

`len(A)`, `A[i]` and iteration run over the region's **vertices**, flattened
across the rings with the outer boundary first, so a region reads like every
other shape. The holes stay reachable through [`holeCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a95fa631cdfb182d4582639f27036ad90 "Returns the number of holes."), [`hole(i)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#a2b6447fb67d376262ab25b4dc5a1e8e5 "Accesses a hole by index.") and
[`holes()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html#ae82e3ee3003e31fd957a88a84d3e6ed9 "Returns the holes in canonical order."), and `point in A` is point containment as everywhere else.

### Polygon Set

The class [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors.") represents a set of
[`PolygonWithHoles`](#polygon-with-holes) components with pairwise disjoint
interiors. The point set is simply their union:

$$A = A_0 \cup A_1 \cup \dots$$

This is the shape that **closes** the regularized
[boolean operations](shape_methods.md#boolean-operations). A difference, a union
or a symmetric difference of two regions can come apart into several pieces, and
an island stranded inside a hole of the answer is a piece like any other — so
before this shape existed those operations had to answer with a bare list, which
could not be fed back in, compared, hashed, drawn or measured.

```python
square = pgl.Polygon([0,0, 10,0, 10,10, 0,10])
holed  = square.difference(pgl.Rectangle(pgl.Point(3,3), pgl.Point(7,7)))
again  = holed.difference(pgl.Rectangle(pgl.Point(0,0), pgl.Point(2,2)))
merged = again.regularizedUnion(holed)
```

It is also the only pypgl shape whose point set **need not be connected**, and
its components are deliberately **not nested**: a component stranded inside
another's hole is stored beside it, not within it.

The components are kept in canonical (sorted) order, so equality, ordering and
hashing do not depend on the order they were supplied in; components of zero area
cover nothing that survives and are dropped, and duplicates are erased. As with
[`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices.") and [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes."), structural validity — every component valid,
component interiors pairwise disjoint, and no two components sharing a stretch of
edge — is a documented precondition rather than an enforced invariant, and
[`isValid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ad94e8914ee4c3146da2fa1e862796d97 "Tests the structural contract: every component valid, component interiors pairwise disjoint, no two components sharing a stretch of edge.") checks it on demand.

A set `A` has methods such as:

- [`A.componentCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ad4d95e2b28c9e5c63373114684cd0354 "Returns the number of components.") / [`A.component(i)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#aa9a5bcd6bc13e3bc2490130482e09839 "Accesses a component by index.") / [`A.components()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a9d7dd4f7e2fc61720d22bea18a399a4f "Returns the components in canonical order."): The components, in canonical order.
- [`A.addComponent(r)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a3971866dab2b17906e8aa896fe13549a "Adds a component, keeping the canonical order.") / [`A.eraseComponent(i)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a6e25a7b16ecacf2902e030baaf00d635 "Erases the component at the given index.") / [`A.eraseComponent(r)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a6e25a7b16ecacf2902e030baaf00d635 "Erases the component at the given index."): Add or remove a component in place; the last returns whether it found one.
- [`A.empty()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a757f15e99380dfe636b26fe7ad89ac8a "Tests whether the set has no components at all."): Returns true if the set has no components at all.
- [`A.isConnected()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a549c618ee865d149f43f6d6549e4cafd "Tests whether the set is connected as a point set."): Returns true if the set is connected as a point set. Two components that never touch are two pieces; the empty set is connected by convention, having nothing to come apart.
- [`A.isPinched()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ad2d4aa1226747fc35ac3abbb8246d7dc "Tests whether two components touch each other anywhere."): Returns true if two components touch each other anywhere. `False` is the cheap exact case: components that stay apart make every relation fold componentwise.
- [`A.isRegular()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a584f3a51697df72e299f9dc6ee313fe7 "Tests whether the set is the closure of its own interior (A = closure(A°)).") / [`A.regularized()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ac041adf6d9991773979e2ff9e040dc66 "Returns the set without its slits (closure(A°))."): A set is regular exactly when every component is, since no slit can run between two components. [`regularized()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ac041adf6d9991773979e2ff9e040dc66 "Returns the set without its slits (closure(A°)).") returns a [`PolygonSet`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html "Set of closed regions with pairwise disjoint interiors."), so the regularization is idempotent in the type system and not only in the mathematics.
- [`A.isValid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ad94e8914ee4c3146da2fa1e862796d97 "Tests the structural contract: every component valid, component interiors pairwise disjoint, no two components sharing a stretch of edge.") / [`A.isSimple()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a0482b932f7f1ef3a8096256c32868280 "Tests whether every ring of every component is simple."): The structural contract above, and the per-ring simplicity check.
- [`A.holeCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ad91325e281eeeb2d893d7e5b1dc2efd8 "Returns the total number of holes over all components.") / [`A.hasHoles()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a62e23d5a9008fe5beac363f92faf254e "Tests whether any component has a hole.") / [`A.vertexCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a735173d08465e2229c3219f0b4e3b911 "Returns the total number of vertices over every ring of every component.") / [`A.vertices()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ac4f23d3e50e18739d63e89628b89db84 "Returns the vertices of every ring of every component.") / [`A.edges()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a298a259daf38720b5f96351a73b165c8 "Returns the boundary edges of every ring of every component.") / [`A.orientedEdges()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#af59e63185d7dc2a4a02635a917fc3c27 "Returns the boundary edges directed so the set lies to the left."): Counted and collected over every ring of every component.
- [`A.area()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ac17f7239d703c2c454cb74d04b6c8e24 "Computes the area of the set.") / [`A.twiceArea()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a2cad2182f1d085898d1b0b4ad1438485 "Computes twice the area of the set.") / [`A.centroid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a12413cbfee7708e42aff80fe8177cc10 "Computes the area-weighted centroid of the set.") / [`A.verticesCentroid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a421b611c3bc590565a06bd7e2cc917fb "Computes the centroid of the vertex set over every ring of every component.") / [`A.pointInside()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ae73e04e11cd03d731461c5bf657492f8 "Returns a point strictly inside the set.") / [`A.diameter()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a42f548b878347ee9ad0b39c9a9c73015 "Returns a segment realizing the diameter (the farthest vertex pair).") / [`A.bbox()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#afd8fd6f8dfdb8842dad379ed1a9f6799 "Computes the bounding box of the set."): The components have disjoint interiors, so the area is simply their sum; the diameter may join two different components.
- [`A.triangulation()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a1a3ddf41a22cf7b71b1f09027eeae314 "Builds the constrained Delaunay triangulation of this set.") / [`A.convexPartition()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#aa04736f7b8528549264d4d196e2b17b2 "Cuts this set into convex pieces with disjoint interiors.") / [`A.convexCovering()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a0a635a70c1f93a7e3c74dc30fb7a7344 "Covers this set with a greedily selected set of convex polygons."): The gaps between components are left out of the domain, exactly as a region's holes are.

`len(A)`, `A[i]` and iteration run over the set's **vertices**, flattened across
every ring of every component, so a set reads like every other shape — the same
choice [`PolygonWithHoles`](#polygon-with-holes) makes. The components stay
reachable through [`componentCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ad4d95e2b28c9e5c63373114684cd0354 "Returns the number of components."), [`component(i)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#aa9a5bcd6bc13e3bc2490130482e09839 "Accesses a component by index.") and [`components()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#a9d7dd4f7e2fc61720d22bea18a399a4f "Returns the components in canonical order."), and
`point in A` is point containment as everywhere else.

Like [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices."), [`Polygon`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Polygon.html "Closed simple polygon stored by its vertices.") and [`PolygonWithHoles`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonWithHoles.html "Closed region bounded by one outer simple polygon minus disjoint polygonal holes."), a set is **mutable and therefore
unhashable**. It can be stored in a [`ShapeTree`](data_structures.md#shape-tree)
and drawn on a [canvas](canvas.md), where it is drawn as one shape however many
pieces it came apart into.

- Other methods: [`boundaryContains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#affc29b801f5b51aaceadaa46a5c5a833 "Tests whether this shape's boundary contains the other shape (∂A ⊇ B)."), [`contains`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1PolygonSet.html#ab95c068a28f7f28a664b4f8308ec1fba "Tests whether this shape contains the other shape (A ⊇ B)."), ### Halfplane Intersection

The class [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.") represents the intersection of a finite set of
closed half-planes: a convex region that, unlike [`Convex`](#convex), may be
unbounded (a wedge, a strip, a half-plane, or the whole plane) and may be empty.

Two conventions are worth pinning down before anything else.

A **default-constructed region is the whole plane** — the intersection of no
half-planes — which is the opposite of `Convex()`, the empty set.

Its **stored elements are half-planes, not points**. The region's corners are
implicit, and generally not representable in the coordinate type of the
half-planes that bound them: integer half-planes routinely bound regions with
rational vertices. That is exactly the case pypgl's single exact rational
instantiation handles without rounding, so [`vertices()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a4a95601bee025101f8267f3827bf5586 "Returns every vertex of the region, in pair-index order (for a bounded region: counterclockwise).") is exact rather than a
rounding step.

```python
k = pgl.HalfplaneIntersection(pgl.Rectangle(pgl.Point(0,0), pgl.Point(4,4)))
len(k), k.vertexCount()      # 4 half-planes, 4 corners
k.intersection(pgl.Rectangle(pgl.Point(2,2), pgl.Point(9,9))).area()
# Output: 4
```

A half-plane intersection `k` has methods such as:

- [`k.insert(h)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#ac1856ebc53281385a995a6bdd43461ec "Intersects the region with one more half-plane."): Intersects the region with one more half-plane, in place. Returns `False` when the half-plane is discarded — because it is redundant, or undefined (a degenerate half-plane bounds no side, so it carries no constraint). When it empties the region, the region switches to a sticky empty state; otherwise it is stored and the stored half-planes it makes redundant are removed.
- [`k.empty()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a3ab10f66c1f39471b44d03eff527b94d "Returns whether the region is the empty set."), [`k.isPlane()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#afece20a10fa322f6450ad3c4691aefba "Returns whether the region is the whole plane (no half-planes)."), [`k.isBounded()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a79271b52491bf5ce89ab26d5ef574e92 "Returns whether the region is bounded."), [`k.isDegenerate()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a7f912f08d9342e92565a52bab98d4ab7 "Returns whether the region has empty interior (it is empty or lower-dimensional: a line, ray, segment, or point)."): State queries. A degenerate region has empty interior — a line, ray, segment, or point built from touching constraints — and remains fully supported by the predicates.
- [`k.isUndefined()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#afd9d78540622355fb2372912daf7d5bc "Returns whether the region is undefined."): Always `False`: [`insert`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#ac1856ebc53281385a995a6bdd43461ec "Intersects the region with one more half-plane.") ignores undefined half-planes, so every region is well defined.
- [`k.isHalfplane()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a42737ebaddd223b85cb5eeeae90d7efd "Returns whether the region is exactly one closed half-plane.") / [`k.getIfHalfplane()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#ab024eed55307be448d59f9870c2895d8 "Returns the half-plane the region equals, if it is one."): Whether the region is exactly one closed half-plane, and that half-plane. Exact, no division.
- [`k.isLine()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#aba67ebe6622f720ad8145c2b69c160f6 "Returns whether the region is exactly one line.") / [`k.getIfLine()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#af835640cfefbadfc98801afd49eea473 "Returns the line the region equals, if it is one."): Whether the region is exactly one line, and that line. Needs no coordinate arithmetic: a degenerate region is a point, segment, ray, or line, and only the line has no vertex.
- [`k.isRay()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#ab9e6c525eb4ceb9fcf4c1d2069ab4320 "Returns whether the region is exactly one ray.") / [`k.getIfRay()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a8cb9592b6463bfabcde8973f8c346b7e "Returns the ray the region equals, if it is one."): Whether the region is a ray, and that ray.
- [`k.isPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#aa6ad3d5cfc8d1dba95bfe4361f94071b "Returns whether the region is a single point.") / [`k.getIfPoint()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#aff9b80cef1d72a3cbc375ee1796fbccf "Returns the point the region collapses to, if it is one.") and [`k.isSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a734541a80aca5a06fbe267ae516e961e "Returns whether the region is a segment of positive length.") / [`k.getIfSegment()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a2cd5edcaaaa610b7726b93b3a35e800d "Returns the segment the region collapses to, if it is one."): The remaining degenerate cases. The tests are exact whatever the region's own coordinate type, so a point whose coordinates are not integral is still recognized.
- Together with [`empty`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a3ab10f66c1f39471b44d03eff527b94d "Returns whether the region is the empty set.") and [`isPlane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#afece20a10fa322f6450ad3c4691aefba "Returns whether the region is the whole plane (no half-planes).") these name every region a half-plane intersection can be, except a full-dimensional one other than a half-plane.
- [`k.vertexCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#aa12330e03c05998ca53a4260cfa2a2e8 "Returns the number of vertices of the region."), [`k.vertex(i)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#af0c6178ec97f95f05ebc7b0a485ea3c6 "Returns the vertex between half-planes i and i+1 (cyclically)."), [`k.vertices()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a4a95601bee025101f8267f3827bf5586 "Returns every vertex of the region, in pair-index order (for a bounded region: counterclockwise)."): The implicit corners, counterclockwise for a bounded region, and exact.
- [`k.edge(i)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#aea13b5f5b8eaf3366a54a1e6630625a7 "Returns the boundary contribution of half-plane i as a typed one-dimensional shape."): The boundary contribution of half-plane `i`: a [`Segment`](#segment) when both neighbouring vertices exist, a [`Ray`](#ray) when only one does, and the whole boundary [`Line`](#line) otherwise.
- [`k.halfplanes()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#ac5bc7e05a70a3492017c261dce72ba62 "Returns a copy of the stored half-planes, in boundary order."): The stored half-planes, in boundary order.
- [`k.bbox()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a00c49cca98cf3ef08461db03296d1e37 "Computes the bounding box of the region."), [`k.asConvex()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a8e0bd5d447292f4da7ab0ba9fbe43d1d "Returns the region as a convex polygon."), [`k.area()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a5a87e38b51277574fbdcdb5abdb82883 "Returns the area of the region."), [`k.twiceArea()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#abfb56afa4a6e986bb0e1bf9e6f8f0806 "Returns twice the area of the region."), [`k.centroid()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#adaca2eca069fb7925fb3af9c5531caba "Returns the centroid of the region."): Raise when the region is empty or unbounded — none of them exists then.
- [`k.intersection(other)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a5da65ca307d0a84216446524765a7a33 "Returns the intersection of the two shapes (A ∩ B), empty when they are disjoint."): Intersecting with a [`Halfplane`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Halfplane.html "Closed half-plane defined by an oriented boundary line."), [`Rectangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Rectangle.html "Axis-aligned rectangle stored by minimum and maximum corners."), [`Triangle`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Triangle.html "Closed triangle stored by three vertices."), [`Convex`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1Convex.html "Closed convex polygon stored by its vertices."), or another [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.") returns another [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty."), so the type is closed under these and the result is exact, with no coordinate divisions. Against the 0D/1D shapes it returns the usual concrete piece.

`len(k)`, `k[i]` and iteration run over the **half-planes**, which are what the
region stores; the corners are reached through [`vertexCount()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#aa12330e03c05998ca53a4260cfa2a2e8 "Returns the number of vertices of the region."), [`vertex(i)`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#af0c6178ec97f95f05ebc7b0a485ea3c6 "Returns the vertex between half-planes i and i+1 (cyclically).") and
[`vertices()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a4a95601bee025101f8267f3827bf5586 "Returns every vertex of the region, in pair-index order (for a bounded region: counterclockwise)."). `point in k` is point containment as everywhere
else.

Equality compares the stored half-planes. For full-dimensional regions the
non-redundant half-planes are a canonical function of the point set, so that is
geometric equality; for degenerate regions the representation is not unique and
equality is representational.

A **bounded** [`HalfplaneIntersection`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html "Intersection of closed half-planes; convex but possibly unbounded or empty.") can be stored in a
[`ShapeTree`](data_structures.md#shapetree) and drawn on a
[canvas](canvas.md); an unbounded one has no [`bbox()`](https://gfonsecabr.github.io/pgl/structpgl_1_1HalfplaneIntersection.html#a00c49cca98cf3ef08461db03296d1e37 "Computes the bounding box of the region.") and so cannot be stored,
though it remains a perfectly good *query* shape.
